title_prefix: amount-from-value's string path is not P
mechanism: Confirmed, with two corrections to the record. Core's AmountFromValue (rpc/util.cpp:98-108) hands value.getValStr() to ParseFixedPoint(text, 8) and only then applies MoneyRange, so "Invalid amount" means the TEXT did not parse and "Amount out of range" means it parsed to a number outside [0, MAX_MONEY]; both are RPC_TYPE_ERROR (-3), as is "Amount is not a number or string". ParseFixedPoint (util/strencodings.cpp:271-360) accepts an optional '-', then a mantissa that is either a single '0' or 1-9 followed by digits, an optional '.' plus at least one digit, an optional e/E with optional sign and at least one digit, and NOTHING else; trailing zeros are tracked separately (ProcessMantissaDigit's mantissa_tzeros) so arbitrarily many of them are legal past the eighth decimal, and the final exponent must land in [0,18) after adding decimals. Ours (src/rpc/amounts.lisp:8-61) hand-parses the string as whole + optional fraction with digit-char-p, caps the fraction at 8 characters, and accepts no sign and no exponent at all; there is no leading-zero rule. Correction 1: the record says Core ACCEPTS "1E8" -- it does not accept it as a value; ParseFixedPoint succeeds (10^16 sat) and MoneyRange then rejects it, so Core answers "Amount out of range" while we answer "Invalid amount". Correction 2: the record's "only the string spelling diverges, numeric JSON amounts take the rational/float branch" understates Core's mechanism -- UniValue keeps a number's RAW TEXT and getValStr() returns it, so in Core the number path IS the string path; it happens not to matter for the probes run here (integer -1, double -1.0d0 and 21000001 all answer "Amount out of range" on both sides), but a fix that only touches the stringp branch leaves the two implementations structurally different.
consequence: Kept at S3. 20 of the 44 spellings probed diverge, in three classes, and none of them makes this node compute a DIFFERENT number for an input both sides accept: for every spelling Core and we both accept, the satoshi value is identical (probed on "1", "0.1", "0", "0.0", "0.00000001", "21000000", "20999999.99999999"). Class 1, we accept what Core refuses: "01" => 100000000, "00.1" => 10000000, "000" => 0. These are permissive, and the value we return is the obvious reading of the text, so no client is paid a different amount than it wrote -- the harm is that a client which relies on the node to reject a malformed amount does not get that rejection here. Class 2, we refuse what Core accepts: every exponent spelling ("1e-8", "0.1e-7", "0.01e-6", "0.19e-6", "1e2", "1e+2", "1.0e1", "0.1e1", "0e0") and every spelling with trailing zeros past the eighth decimal ("0.0000000100000000", "0.00000001000000", "1.10000000000000000"). This is fail-safe -- the call errors instead of moving the wrong money -- but a client that formats amounts to 16 or 18 decimals, which is the common way to print a fixed-point value, is refused outright on amounts Core takes; Core's own unit tests pin "0.00000001000000" == 1 and "0.19e-6" == 19 (rpc_tests.cpp:306-307) and "1.10000000000000000" (util_tests.cpp:948). Class 3, the two messages are swapped: "-1", "-0.00000001", "-0" and "1E8" get "Invalid amount" where Core says "Amount out of range", and "10000000000" and "92233720368.54775808" get "Amount out of range" where Core's mantissa/exponent overflow says "Invalid amount". wallet_basic.py:430 asserts -3 "Amount out of range" for sendtoaddress(addr, "-1") -- a string -- so that one is a direct Core-parity failure, and wallet_basic.py:322-325, wallet_bumpfee.py:138,147 and wallet_send.py:341,351 distinguish the same two texts. No money is misdirected, so this stays below S2.
evidence: Two probes. (1) A faithful Python port of ParseFixedPoint + MoneyRange transcribed line by line from refs/bitcoin/src/util/strencodings.cpp:252-360 and consensus/amount.h:27, checked against Core's own vectors (it reproduces every BOOST_CHECK in util_tests.cpp:935-985 and every AmountFromValue case in rpc_tests.cpp:285-313, including "1e-8"=1, "0.19e-6"=19, ".19e-6" invalid, "92233720368.54775808" invalid). (2) build/ga11v/p-amount.lisp (worktree fix/ga11v-rpcutil-s3a, warm image), bl.rpc::amount-from-value over 44 spellings. Divergences, ours | Core: "1e-8" -3 "Invalid amount" | ok 1; "0.1e-7" invalid | ok 1; "0.01e-6" invalid | ok 1; "0.19e-6" invalid | ok 19; "1e2" invalid | ok 10000000000; "1e+2" invalid | ok 10000000000; "1.0e1" invalid | ok 1000000000; "0.1e1" invalid | ok 100000000; "0e0" invalid | ok 0; "0.0000000100000000" invalid | ok 1; "0.00000001000000" invalid | ok 1; "1.10000000000000000" invalid | ok 110000000; "01" ok 100000000 | Invalid amount; "00.1" ok 10000000 | Invalid amount; "000" ok 0 | Invalid amount; "-1" Invalid amount | Amount out of range; "-0.00000001" Invalid amount | Amount out of range; "-0" Invalid amount | ok 0; "1E8" Invalid amount | Amount out of range; "10000000000" Amount out of range | Invalid amount; "92233720368.54775808" Amount out of range | Invalid amount. Agreeing controls, so the probe is not reporting a blanket difference: "1", "0.1", "0", "0.0", "0.00000001", "21000000", "20999999.99999999" all ok with identical values; "21000001" Amount out of range on both; "", "-", ".1", "1.", " 1", "1 ", "1e", "+1", "abc", "0.000000001", "1e-9", "0.1e-9", "1e10", "1e17", "1e18" Invalid amount on both. Error CODE is -3 on both sides everywhere, and non-string non-number input gives -3 "Amount is not a number or string" as Core does. Numeric contrast: integer -1, double -1.0d0 and integer 21000001 all answer -3 "Amount out of range", matching Core. Files: src/rpc/amounts.lisp:8-61; refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/util.cpp:98-108; refs/bitcoin/src/util/strencodings.cpp:252-360; refs/bitcoin/src/consensus/amount.h:27.
fix_shape: Replace the stringp branch with a direct transcription of ParseFixedPoint and let it own the whole function, as Core does. Add PARSE-FIXED-POINT (text decimals) to src/rpc/amounts.lisp returning an integer or NIL, written as a single left-to-right scan over the string in Core's order -- optional '-', then a single '0' or a 1-9 mantissa run, then optional '.' plus at least one digit, then optional e/E with optional sign and at least one digit, then a hard trailing-garbage check -- carrying Core's mantissa_tzeros counter so trailing zeros do not consume precision, and applying Core's four overflow gates against UPPER_BOUND = 10^18-1 and the exponent range [0,18). Then AMOUNT-FROM-VALUE becomes Core's three lines: reject a non-number non-string with "Amount is not a number or string", call PARSE-FIXED-POINT and raise "Invalid amount" on NIL, then raise "Amount out of range" when bl.val:money-range-p is false -- all three at +rpc-type-error+, which is what we already use. To match Core's number path as well, feed the parser the raw TEXT of a JSON number rather than a Lisp float: that means the JSON layer keeping each number's source text alongside the parsed value, which is a larger change and can be staged behind the string fix, but until it happens the current float branch's tolerance slack should be left alone rather than widened, since it is the only thing standing in for Core's exact decimal parse. Test it with Core's own vectors as a table: every BOOST_CHECK from util_tests.cpp:935-985 and every AmountFromValue line from rpc_tests.cpp:285-313, asserting the message text and not just that an error was signalled, plus wallet_basic.py:430's string "-1" => "Amount out of range" driven through dispatch-rpc-method.
